name: Toxic Maculopathy Due to Antimalarial Drugs

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: American Academy of Ophthalmology (AAO) Screening Guidelines for Hydroxychloroquine Retinopathy

criteria.description: History of chronic use of antimalarial drugs (chloroquine or hydroxychloroquine) at or above recommended doses
Presence of characteristic paracentral or pericentral visual field defects on automated perimetry
Abnormalities on retinal imaging such as spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT) showing parafoveal photoreceptor loss or fundus autofluorescence changes
Abnormal multifocal electroretinogram (mfERG) findings consistent with macular dysfunction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Chronic antimalarial drug use plus at least two major criteria including characteristic visual field defects and imaging abnormalities
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Early detection is critical to prevent irreversible vision loss; screening recommended after 5 years of therapy or earlier if risk factors present.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic visual field defect near the central vision
Distinctive retinal pigment epithelium pattern seen on fundus examination

common.notes: Gradual reduction in sharpness of vision
Color vision abnormalities, especially blue-yellow defects

occasional.notes: Difficulty seeing in low light conditions

rare.symptomName: Retinal pigment epithelial atrophy beyond macula
rare.notes: Peripheral retinal changes in advanced cases
searchTerms: damage to retinal pigment layer beyond center

imaging: Spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT) showing parafoveal photoreceptor layer thinning
Visual field testing revealing paracentral scotomas
other: Multifocal electroretinogram (mfERG) abnormalities indicating macular dysfunction

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of drusen and geographic atrophy
Genetic testing positive for known mutations

redFlags: Rapid progression of central vision loss despite drug cessation
Bilateral bull's-eye maculopathy on fundus exam
Visual field defects in patients on long-term antimalarial therapy
references: Marmor MF, Kellner U, Lai TY, Melles RB, Mieler WF. Recommendations on Screening for Chloroquine and Hydroxychloroquine Retinopathy (2016 Revision). Ophthalmology. 2016 Jun;123(6):1386-1394.
American Academy of Ophthalmology. Preferred Practice Pattern® Guidelines. Hydroxychloroquine and Chloroquine Retinopathy Screening. 2016.
Melles RB, Marmor MF. The risk of toxic retinopathy in patients on long-term hydroxychloroquine therapy. JAMA Ophthalmol. 2014 Dec;132(12):1453-1460.
